You can only receive commands from allies who are in your visible minimap area or when the target of the command is in that area.
The overview map is used to get a tactical and strategic view of the whole battlefield. When the overview map is opened, communications from the whole team can be received and messages can be sent.

Recovery was introduced to self-destruct a vehicle that is stuck in the terrain. This mechanic is needed because the increased battle duration and respawn possibility call for the permanent engagement of the player.

Every few minutes, one vehicle is added to your reserve. The reserve can hold a maximum of two vehicles. When there are no vehicles left, you cannot deploy and need to wait until new vehicles are delivered.

the order of unlocking Combat Reserves depends on the vehicle type. One Combat Reserve is available from the start, while others unlock upon reaching the Sergeant and Lieutenant ranks, respectively.

In the <font color='#E9E2BF'>Twist of Fate</font> scenario, purchasing a Combat Reserve will increase its level by one and provide the opportunity to improve it to Level <font color='#E9E2BF'>IV</font>.
A Combat Reserve placed in this slot increases the chance of it being offered in the <font color='#E9E2BF'>Twist of Fate</font> scenario by <font color='#E9E2BF'>10%</font>.
Unlocking and Improving Reserves in Battle
Combat Reserves are unlocked and improved in battle, depending on the vehicle type and rank you reach.

after unlocking all Combat Reserves upon reaching new ranks, these Combat Reserves are improved. The initially unlocked Combat Reserve can be improved up to Level III, and the second unlocked Combat Reserve can be improved up to Level II.
